# Original network scenario cards — Unit 3
Use synthetic diagrams and reason from evidence. No commands, captures or school configuration changes.
N1: remote server’s IP is correct, but client uses its own MAC as frame destination. Explain the required next-hop frame destination.
N2: a learner says both ordinary switches change TTL. Correct with the hop trace.
N3: file bytes arrive out of order/lost; the application needs a complete ordered file. Justify transport recovery requirements, not absolute delivery promises.
N4: a live voice application can handle missing samples but late samples are useless. Explain why a datagram-based design could fit and what the application must still handle.
N5: DNS over TCP appears in a supplied trace. Explain why it does not automatically indicate an invalid DNS implementation.
N6: a learner equates a TCP checksum with encrypted traffic. Distinguish corruption detection, transport recovery and confidentiality.
N7: empty TCP payload yields an alleged 58-byte Ethernet frame in the stated model. Identify missing padding and correct the calculation.
N8: a tracer treats ACK 1041 as 1041 acknowledged packets. Explain byte sequencing using the 40-byte example.
